newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon freezes reduction in clothing tariff.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon freezes reduction in clothing tariff.

text.p: The Lebanese government has put on hold a decision to cut import duties on clothing following a storm of protest from industrialists about the cut, a top industrialist said on Friday.
"Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri has put the decree on hold," Jack Sarraf, President of the Association of Lebanese Industrialists, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Sarraf, who had earlier said he had offered his resignation to the association in protest at the government's decision, said his resignation was now on hold.
"My resignation is now on hold just as the decree is on hold," he said.

He had announced his resignation after five years as president of the association after the government last week cut duties on imported clothing to 20 percent from 30 percent, reversing an increase in duties it had imposed a year earlier.

Sarraf complained on Thursday that many Lebanese clothing manufacturers who had imported capital machinery last year on the strength of the increased import duties would be more vulnerable to foreign competition after the government reduced duties again.
Other leaders of the industrialists association also threatened mass resignation if the government insisted on slashing import duties on clothes.
Sarraf said Hariri told a delegation of industrialists on Friday that a committee grouping the ministers of finance, economy and industry would soon propose new measures to resolve the issue.
"It was an error and we want to coordinate to fix the error," he said.
The reduction in duties angered industrialists because it benefited Asian and Egyptian products that compete directly with Lebanese clothing manufacturers as well as luxury clothing.
Sarraf said Lebanon has 2,000 factories manufacturing clothes, the country's biggest industry.

"We want to become a second Hong Kong. We are for reducing custom duties on almost all 200 categories of imported items. Out of these only 25 categories represent items produced locally," Sarraf said.
"We are not against abolishing duty tariffs on watches and electronics, but not shoes and clothes," he said.
